messages:
maya: quick brain-dump — we need a safe pattern for coordinated burst fallbacks when Dedicated pools hit ephemeral depletion. idea: 1) consume tenant burst tokens, 2) model-downgrade to quantized variant, 3) spill to regional spare capacity, 4) finally preemptible/backfill lane. this order keeps latency & cost predictable.

jonathan: can you paste a rough proto or config sketch? curious how we express priorities + TTLs.

maya: sure — sketch below:
```
fallback_policy:
  - name: burst_tokens
    action: admit_if_tokens
    ttl: 30s
  - name: quantized_downgrade
    action: route_to_model
    model_suffix: ".q4"
    max_latency_increase_ms: 50
  - name: regional_spill
    action: route_region
    regions: ["us-west-2","us-east-1"]
    cost_multiplier: 1.4
  - name: preemptible_lane
    action: schedule_preemptible
    max_queue_ms: 200
```

liam: main worry = burst_tokens can be gamed and cause cost spikes if we don't rate-limit refill. also bookkeeping for tokens across operator restarts.

sarah: agree. recommend token refill tied to usage smoothing window (exponential decay), plus a global budget cap per tenant. soft-queue requests that exceed token rate instead of immediate downgrade.

jonathan: operator boundary Q: who should make the downgrade decision? runtime path (fast, local) or control-plane (policy verification + audit)?

maya: runtime needs to be the fast path for immediate SLOs. control-plane owns policy config, sim/verify, and accepting exceptions. runtime enforces the policy locally (policy blob signed by control-plane). audit events get shipped back.

ops-bot: deploy-bot triggered: fallback-policy-v1 config pushed to canary (10% traffic) by maya at 6298765444.

liam: for observability, we need metrics: fallback.invocations{kind=burst_tokens|quantized|spill|preemptible}, fallback.latency_delta_ms, fallback.cost_impact_estimate, tenant.burst_token_balance. these must be exposed with per-tenant cardinality control.

jonathan: also add histogram for time-between-fallbacks for the same tenant — helps detect oscillation.

maya: +1. test plan: enable canary (10%), run synthetic spike generator simulating 5x baseline for 3m, measure: latency tail, downgrade rate, and cost spread. if downgrade_rate > 20% for dedicated-sla-tenants -> automatic rollback.

sarah: how do we respect Dedicated SLAs? we shouldn't downgrade a tenant that purchased a 'no-downgrade' policy.

maya: SLA hierarchy:
- hard SLA (no-downgrade): only spill to region or preemptible lane under operator approval
- soft SLA (default dedicated): allow quantized downgrade + burst token consumption
- best-effort: full fallback sequence allowed
we need explicit flags on tenant profile.

liam: implementation nit: keep downgrade logic pluggable per model family. some Llama-like variants have worse quality drop with q4; don't auto-quantize if quality loss > threshold.

jonathan: sounds good. question on correctness: when we 'spill to regional spare capacity' how do we guarantee prefix cache warmness? cold cache could blow latency.

maya: two mitigations: 1) pre-warm KV cache for active tenants in the spill target (cheap async warmers), 2) prefer spill targets with recent traffic affinity first. also expose a 'spill_latency_penalty' metric so routing can prefer the least-bad option.

ops-bot: incident-bot notice: reminder to coordinate with eng-sre if canary crosses 100 requests/s.

jonathan: last: rollback story — add an explicit kill-switch at control-plane, and the runtime will honor emergency-policy: "no-fallback" TTL until cleared. simple and effective.

maya: agreed. next steps: I'll open an RFC follow-up with the sketch + detailed telemetry table and experiment plan. tagging @jonathan @liam @sarah for review. :thumbsup:
